copy.step0_intro_0: Have you ever wondered how birds can flap their wings hard enough to fly, but their feathers don't blow apart in all that wind?
copy.step0_intro_1: You need to look at a feather real close. It has all these little ridges in neat rows. Those are called barbs.
copy.step0_intro_2: And the reason all those barbs don't pull apart from each other is because they have tiny HOOKS! Those hooks, called barbules, hold the whole feather together! Neat, huh?
copy.step0_intro_3: Hey, go find a feather and look for the barbs. They're easy to see. The hooks, or barbules, are too small to see; but they're there! Want to look at a feather?
copy.step0_summary: Kit wants you to find a feather and look at the rows of barbs, all held in place by tiny hooks called barbules.
